tool.scope: pipe A planes 1-3 requested writes at the WEX wrapper; not a hardware latch proof

static.note: syncPlaneUpdates only changes CTL bit3 (arm marker); it does not decide async. The flip transaction +0x2C bit0 or controller/path feature bytes select the synchronous CTL.

candidate.effect: clear PLANE_CTL bit9 on writes to 0x70180/0x71180/0x72180 only; preserve bit3 and all other bits
candidate.publication: TGLNoAsyncFlip = [enabled, suppressed] on a type-1 framebuffer client open

established_host: During the UU window the primary plane used async address updates; the idle and GRD windows did not.
No pipe A FIFO underrun was reported by the unmasked native chain or the WEX bit31 ACK path in any capture.
Around all 23 manual UU marks there was no plane enable/disable, position/size change, DDB/buf_cfg change, or observation-ring loss.
All fast same-buffer reuses in the UU capture were at full plane setups, not steady-state shallow reuse.
No overlay plane was in use; the primary plane covered the full 2560x1440 screen.
not_proven: That async address update is the cause of the user-visible flicker.
That the UU/GRD difference is due to async rather than the application, its frame/content cadence, or the 829 full plane setups seen only in UU.
That clearing bit9 removes the artifact; the candidate is not installed and has no hardware A/B.
That the manual marks align with a specific flip; marks are -2 s/+0.5 s windows, not frame-synchronized.

confounders: UU updated at 60.39 SURF/s with 829 full plane setups; GRD at 20.76 SURF/s with none. This is not a strict single-variable comparison.
The two applications differ in decoder, renderer and surface presentation; content-level corruption cannot be excluded without synchronized capture.
The GRD capture had no manual marks, consistent with the user's report but not an independent pixel proof.
The candidate only covers direct PLANE_CTL writes through WEX's register-write wrappers; the trigger-packet path is not converted. No LPVP shadow register 0x70680 was observed in this capture.
